pageCache.pageTitle: Wrap Around Provision | Old Palace & Children's House Nursery School Federation
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
This provision is designed to offer general childcare support for both working and non-working parents. Sessions will run Monday to Thursday, during term time only, from 3:30pm to 5:45pm.
During each session, children will take part in a range of fun and engaging activities, delivered in line with our school Health & Safety guidance.
After reviewing local provision, we have found that most schools in Tower Hamlets charge approximately £10 per session, per child. This reflects the average cost of delivering quality care and activities. To help families during the cost, we will be charging £8 per session, per child.
In order to use the wrap around service, we kindly ask that you email the school a week in advance with the day required for childcare.
If you would like further information, please do not hesitate to contact the school office.

Nursery Admissions
CHILDREN’S HOUSE ARE NOW ACCEPTING APPLICATIONS
FOR 2, 3 & 4 YEAR OLDS FOR SEPTEMER 2026
Statement for admissionsStarting nursery school is a big moment for you and your child. We want your child to have the best start in life and are here to answer any questions you may have, to help you find the right nursery place.
At Children’s House Nursery School, children who qualify for a place may access a morning place 9am-12pm or an afternoon place 12.30-3.30pm.
We follow the admissions procedures outlined in the Local Authority’s “Starting Nursery in Tower Hamlets Booklet”This booklet can be accessed by clicking on the link.
Please pop into the school office between 10am-2pm or telephone Sabiya on 0208 980 4662A paper copy is available from the Local Authority’s Pupil Admissions Team on 020 7364 5006
All three and four year olds are entitled to 15 hours of free early years education per week and this is available from the term after their third birthday.
How decisions are made
The pupil service team processes applications and coordinates decisions for those who apply.The local authority in accordance with the admission criteria below makes the decisions on applications for Tower Hamlets nursery schools:
Thirty-Hour PlacesEligible parents may be entitled to an additional 15 hours nursery education a week.You can check your eligibility at for the Government’s 30 hour place at www.childcarechoices.gov.uk If eligible you can then let the school office know your 11-digit code.Alternatively you can telephone the HMRC helpline on 0300 123 4097
Two-Year-Old PlacesChildren’s House Nursery School offers places to eligible two year olds.Some parents of two year olds are eligible for 15 hours free nursery education for their two year old but must meet certain government (income based) criteria.
You can check your eligibility at https://www.gov.uk/help-with-childcare-costs/free-childcare-2-year-olds
Visiting Children’s HouseWe warmly invite you to visit Children’s House to see for yourself the wonderful experiences on offer.You can arrange a visit by calling the school office on: 020 8980 4662

pageCache.pageTitle: Childrens House History | Old Palace & Children's House Nursery School Federation
pageCache.text:
We are 100 Years Old ​”Childhood – Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow”
Children’s House Nursery School opened on 24 October 1923.
​The founders, Doris and Muriel Lester worked tirelessly as social reformers, pacifists and non-conformists.It was Doris’ dream to build a school for the children of Bow, based on Maria Montessori’s pedagogy. “Nothing is too good for the children of Bow!” said Doris Lester of the community.
The first stone was laid in a ceremony on 11 April 1923 and the school was opened later that year by writer, HG Wells.
The current Children’s House community remain so proud of our school. Marking our 100th year, we looked at photographs and documents that have been preserved and handed down and a few tears have been shed just recognising the long history this fantastic school has had on the community. We would love to hear from previous pupils, families, staff and members of the community: we are currently collating memories, thoughts and photographs.
In Summer 2025 we gathered all the wonderful historical documentation that we had at Children’s House, some of which dated back to 1925. We invited Richard Wiltshire from Tower Hamlets Archives to come and help select pieces to be transferred across for safekeeping in the archives at Bancroft Road. Photographs, school records, children’s work and historic and pedagogical policies as well as the founder’s parchment were safely transported to be stored securely. The documents will be available for viewing in time and generations to come will know the impact our school has had on communities in Bow and beyond.
Also enjoy our blog which documents our wonderful Centenary Party on 29 June 2024 by clicking here. In the meantime, please enjoy the incredible photographs and articles, some of which date back 100 years.What has struck our wonderful team working here now, is our principles are still the same as Doris and Muriel back in 1923 and we are so grateful to them for their vision.
​There is more information about our founders here.

The Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum
The Early Years Foundation Stage Framework is mandatory for all early years providers, maintained schools, non-maintained schools, independent schools, and all providers on the Early Years Register. The EYFS Statutory Framework sets the standards that all early years providers must meet to ensure that children learn and develop well and are kept healthy and safe. It promotes teaching and learning and gives children the broad range of knowledge and skills that provide the right foundation for today and good future progress through school and life beyond school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding | Old Palace & Children's House Nursery School Federation
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
Safeguarding and promoting the wellbeing of children is everyone’s responsibility.
The school has a legal duty of care for the health, safety, security and wellbeing of all pupils and staff. Children’s House is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and requires all staff, volunteers and visitors to share this commitment.
If you notice anything that you feel is a cause for concern, relating to a child’s safety in our school, please ensure you discuss it immediately with a member of the safeguarding team, listed below:
Child-Protection-Policy-2025
The school has been given the opportunity to take part in a project that will run jointly between schools and the Metropolitan Police. Operation Encompass directly connects the police with the school to ensure support for children when there has been (a police attended) incident of domestic abuse. Operation Encompass provides an efficient, confidential channel of communication between the police force and the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) at the school. This is to ensure that the school are able to make provision for possible difficulties experienced by children, or their families, who have been involved in, or exposed to, a domestic abuse incident. We are keen to offer the best support possible to all our pupils and we believe this will be extremely beneficial for all those involved.
Guthsna Khan is the Designated Safeguarding Lead.
Mirka Mahon is a Designated Safeguarding Officer.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Dinners | Old Palace & Children's House Nursery School Federation
pageCache.text:
Packed Lunches
We know how important it is to ensure children have a positive experience of eating together. At Children’s House children enjoy their lunch in a family style service. They eat in their classroom with their friends. Children help set the table and clear it away afterwards. Sensitive and supportive adults help the children to serve their lunches.
Children’s House operate as a packed lunch only school. If your child stays all day, please provide a healthy packed lunch.
All children have access to fresh water and milk and are encouraged to enjoy their food, try something new and exchange chat during a sociable experience. We also have an independent table in each room where children can serve themselves and manage their own needs.
Lunch is a calm and enjoyable experience at Children’s House and the high expectations of our staff ensure our Children’s House Values are supported during this time.

pageCache.text:
School Uniform
The uniform consists of the following:
For illustration purposes, please refer to uniform gallery below.
It is also essential that the children bring a waterproof coat/jacket each day, so they will remain dry in the event of wet weather. These need to be suitable for school.
In colder weather, the need for good ventilation may mean that rooms are cooler. Therefore children should be encouraged to provide layers, which can be added/ taken off as the temperature changes.
When children participate in Physical Education lessons, children must change for all activities. Articles worn indoors must include plimsolls, shorts and a T-shirt. In colder weather children may wear a sweatshirt, jumper or fleece. Head scarves must either be removed or replaced with a bandana before the start of the lesson. The PE kit should consist of:
The school advises that pupils bring in a PE bag at the start of the week and take this home at the end of the week. This will help to ensure that pupils always have suitable footwear available to change into when undertaking physical activity.
Non-Uniform days & School Parties
On occasions, pupils are allowed to wear clothes other than the school uniform. This may include non-uniform days to raise money and awareness for charities, during Christmas and Eid parties, on World Book Day or when on school trips. This is always at the discretion of the school.
Whilst this allows pupils the opportunity to express themselves as individuals, it must be done so in an appropriate way. It is particularly important that any pupil dress on these occasions recognises that the school is still a working environment, is practical and safe and does not cause embarrassment or offence to staff, pupils and other members of the school community.
For example – but not exhaustively:
The final decision on the suitability of clothes and their compliance with this policy is down to the school’s Leadership Team

Black or grey trousers or skirt
Plain black, grey or white socks.
Plain black shoes
PLAIN T-shirt
PLAIN shorts or tracksuit bottoms
Black plimsolls (indoor)

No offensive clothing;
No revealing clothing;
No clothing that causes embarrassment;
No clothing that gives rise to misunderstanding;
No political or contentious slogans;
Nothing discriminatory;
No jewellery, make-up, face paints or transfers
LEGAL DUTIES UNDER THE EQUALITY ACT 2010
The Equality Act 2010 prohibits discrimination against an individual based on the protected characteristics, which include sex, race, religion or belief, and gender reassignment.
